purpose: Rebalance human evidence by adding independent null and negative human evidence, which remained underrepresented after Extension 11 recount.
source_policy: Every record has a PubMed PMID verified before inclusion. Evidence text is curator-written from the PubMed abstract and explicitly not verbatim.
overlap_policy: All 12 PMIDs are unique and have zero overlap with the 82 human-evidence PMIDs already present in the uploaded project.

records.title: A randomized controlled trial of the effect of fluid extract of Echinacea purpurea on the incidence and severity of colds and respiratory infections
records.indication: prevention and severity of colds/respiratory infections
records.evidence_text: The trial found no statistically significant difference between Echinacea and placebo in the number, duration, or severity of colds and respiratory infections.

records.title: Effect of silymarin (milk thistle) on liver disease in patients with chronic hepatitis C unsuccessfully treated with interferon therapy: a randomized controlled trial
records.evidence_text: Neither tested silymarin dose differed from placebo on the prespecified ALT response, HCV RNA, or quality-of-life outcomes.

records.title: Kava for generalised anxiety disorder: A 16-week double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study
records.evidence_text: The phase III trial found a non-significant difference in anxiety reduction between kava and placebo.

records.title: Safety and efficacy of dietary supplement (gintonin-enriched fraction from ginseng) in subjective memory impairment: A randomized placebo-controlled trial
records.evidence_text: There was no between-group difference in the primary or secondary cognitive outcome changes after eight weeks.

records.title: Effects of Korean Red Ginseng on Cognitive and Motor Function: A Double-blind, Randomized, Placebo-controlled Trial
records.indication: cognitive performance in healthy young adults
records.evidence_text: The trial found no significant differences between red ginseng and placebo in the Vienna cognitive test system scores.

records.title: Treatment of anxiety, tension and restlessness states with Kava special extract WS 1490 in general practice: a randomized placebo-controlled double-blind multicenter trial
records.evidence_text: The prespecified post-treatment comparison on the primary anxiety rating did not show a statistically significant difference between kava and placebo.

records.title: Valerian does not appear to reduce symptoms for patients with chronic insomnia in general practice using a series of randomised n-of-1 trials
records.evidence_text: Valerian was not shown to be appreciably better than placebo for sleep or sleep-related outcomes in individual patients or the group overall.

records.title: Hawthorn Extract Randomized Blinded Chronic Heart Failure (HERB CHF) trial
records.indication: chronic heart failure symptoms and functional capacity
records.evidence_text: Hawthorn provided no symptomatic or functional benefit when added to standard medical therapy for chronic heart failure.

records.title: Milk thistle for the treatment of liver disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
records.evidence_text: The review found no reduction in mortality and no clinically meaningful improvement in liver histology or biochemical markers sufficient to support recommending milk thistle for liver disease.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of echinacea in treating upper respiratory tract infections in children: a randomized controlled trial
records.indication: upper respiratory tract infections in children
records.evidence_text: Echinacea did not reduce illness duration or symptom severity in children and was associated with an increased risk of rash.

records.title: An internet-based randomized, placebo-controlled trial of kava and valerian for anxiety and insomnia
records.evidence_text: Neither kava for anxiety nor valerian for insomnia relieved symptoms more than placebo.

records.title: Kava in generalized anxiety disorder: three placebo-controlled trials
records.evidence_text: Across three controlled trials and pooled analyses, no efficacy signal for kava was found and the authors concluded that the findings did not support its use for generalized anxiety disorder.
